clue.text: Hard setback for footballer selfish type

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
an own goal, OG, is the worst setback a footballer can inflict on their own side

explanation.surface: A tough defender suffers a setback, scoring against his own team while playing selfishly.
explanation.walkthrough: OG, short for own goal, is a football term: a player knocking the ball into their own net.
explanation.definitionFit: A greedy person who keeps everything for themselves is called a pig, or by the farmyard synonym used here.

clue.text: Man with unpredictable date, a singer, figure of authority for youngsters?

parts.note: he stands for a man

indicators.note: unpredictable says the letters of date are rearranged

parts.note: Cher is the American pop singer

explanation.surface: A man with a fickle date, a pop singer, is the sort children look up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unpredictable' rearranges DATE to ADTE. The surface pairs a man with 'a singer', but the A belongs to the singer: a Cher.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a school has authority over its pupils.

clue.text: German revolutionary acquiring liberal honour to travel widely

indicators.note: acquiring means the other pieces take the liberal and honour inside them

parts.note: a Trot is a Trotskyist revolutionary
an OBE is a British honour, Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A German radical picks up a liberal decoration so as to tour the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquiring' means the German revolutionary takes the liberal honour inside. A Trot is a dated name for a follower of Trotsky; the OBE is a British award, Officer of the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: To journey around the planet is to roam across it, visiting many countries.

clue.text: Dull quality in dodgy casino featuring in papers

indicators.note: featuring in tells us the rearranged letters sit inside the word for papers

parts.note: the papers collectively are the press

indicators.note: dodgy suggests something unreliable or crooked, so the letters of casino are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a shady gambling house turns out to be tedious reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' makes OSAICN, and 'featuring in' sets it inside the papers' word. 'Dull quality' is a noun phrase, fitting the -NESS ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means commonplace and unimaginative, so the noun names a lack of flair or excitement.

clue.text: Outstanding bishop taken in by Arab organisation harmless stuff?

indicators.note: taken in by means these letters go inside the organisation

parts.note: PLO is the Palestine Liberation Organization
ace means excellent or outstanding
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A distinguished bishop is captured by an Arab group, though they are harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' means the organisation swallows the other pieces. The question mark marks the definition as playful: a dummy pill does nothing, harmful or otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill with no active ingredient is given in trials; it is inert, so does no harm.

clue.text: Simple legal matter requiring order to traveller at customs?

definitions.meaning: a court case so clear-cut that its outcome is obvious
read literally, a customs officer telling someone to unzip and then close their luggage

explanation.surface: A straightforward lawsuit involving instructions to someone arriving through customs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a matter easily decided; literally, it instructs a passenger to unfasten then fasten their bag.

clue.text: Gnarled sort acclaims endlessly hard seasonal work

indicators.note: gnarled means twisted and knotted, so the letters are twisted into a new order
endlessly means the last letter of hard is dropped

explanation.surface: A crusty old type cheers without end something tough at this time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts HARD to HAR, and 'Gnarled' rearranges SORT, ACCLAIMS and HAR together.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Christmas story is a work tied to one festive season.

clue.text: A leader of gangsters among one of many brothers formerly-found here?

indicators.note: among means the following letters are placed inside the brother's name

parts.note: Chico was one of the Marx Brothers, the comedy family

indicators.note: leader of picks the first letter of gangsters

explanation.surface: A gang boss in the company of a brother: this is where such men used to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' sets A and G, from 'leader of', inside the brother's name. The hyphen joins 'formerly-found here' as one definition: 1920s gangsters such as Capone made this city notorious.
explanation.definitionFit: The American city on Lake Michigan was notorious for Prohibition-era mobsters such as Capone.

clue.text: Poet and priest with holy books

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Old Testament book of Samuel
OT is the Old Testament, a set of holy books

explanation.surface: A poet goes about with a clergyman and some scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli, the priest who raised Samuel, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: T S Eliot wrote The Waste Land and is among the best-known modern poets.

clue.text: Make out mole

definitions.meaning: to make out is to discern or catch sight of something
a mole is a secret agent inside an organisation

explanation.surface: Discern a burrowing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To glimpse something is to discern it; an undercover agent is a mole.

clue.text: Odour recalled in team or association

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A smell brings back memories of a sports team or club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' tells you to read backwards the letters AMORA that run across 'teAM OR Association'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant smell or scent is an odour, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Race shown in film close to North Belfast maybe

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's famous film about an extraterrestrial

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of North is taken

parts.note: Belfast is an example of a Northern Ireland city, NI plus CITY

explanation.surface: A racial theme is explored in a movie set near north Belfast.
explanation.walkthrough: NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland, so Belfast is an NI CITY; 'maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnicity is the state of belonging to a particular racial or cultural group.

clue.text: Easter breaks around end of month — and May?

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the extra letter
breaks means the word Easter is broken up and its letters rearranged
end of picks the last letter of month

explanation.surface: Easter holidays fall round the end of the month, and there is May too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' rearranges EASTER, and 'around' wraps those letters around H, the last letter of 'month' ('end of'). The '— and May?' tail turns the month into a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The former British Prime Minister whose surname was May had this first name.

clue.text: Short rest taken in country ignoring central character in an awkward way

indicators.note: taken in means the rest is placed inside the shortened country
ignoring central character means the middle letter of the country is dropped

parts.note: Italy is the country
a nap is a brief sleep or short rest

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a quick nap abroad and ends up behaving clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring central character' drops the middle letter A to leave ITLY, and 'taken in' places the rest within it. 'Short rest' is one phrase for the nap, not a cue to shorten anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or clumsy, so the adverb describes acting awkwardly or inappropriately.

clue.text: European once valuing soya possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Someone who prizes soya beans is perhaps from somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges VALUING SOYA; 'once' marks a country that no longer exists.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balkan federation broke up in the 1990s, so a citizen of it was a European of a former state.

clue.text: Proviso during broadcast for modern office feature?

indicators.note: during means the proviso comes in the middle of the broadcast word

parts.note: an airing is a broadcast on radio or television
a proviso is a condition attached to an agreement

explanation.surface: A stipulation made on air about what a contemporary workplace should have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' sets the proviso inside the broadcast word. The question mark warns that the definition names an example rather than a dictionary meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate control that cools the air is a standard fitting in today's workplaces, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Boozer, English catholic, to feel regret missing opening in urban heartland

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub, an inn
RC stands for Roman Catholic

indicators.note: missing opening means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to pity is to feel sorrow or regret for someone

explanation.surface: A pub-goer, English and Catholic, is sorry to be away from the heart of town.
explanation.walkthrough: A boozer is British slang for a pub. 'missing opening' drops the P from PITY to leave ITY.
explanation.definitionFit: The central, often deprived, districts of a big town form its core.

clue.text: For the most part shined in order to receive prominent attention

annotationWithheld.clue: For the most part shined in order to receive prominent attention

clue.text: Greek ambassador harbouring woman

indicators.note: harbouring means the ambassador's letters shelter the woman's name

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
Ellen is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An envoy gives shelter to a woman from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbouring' shelters the woman inside the ambassador's letters; an ambassador is styled His Excellency.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hellene is an inhabitant of Hellas, the Greek name for Greece.

clue.text: Current measure embraced by fat footballer

indicators.note: embraced by means the unit sits inside the word for fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat
an amp is the unit for measuring electric current

explanation.surface: A footballer is caught up in some greasy electrical business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' puts the measure inside the fat. Frank Lampard is a former Chelsea and England midfielder.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Lampard played for Chelsea and England, so the surname names a footballer.

clue.text: Poor service after getting bit of jewellery and lock

indicators.note: after means the service word comes behind the jewellery word

parts.note: a ring is a piece of jewellery
in tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and must be replayed

explanation.surface: A tennis player serves badly after being given a piece of jewellery and a padlock.
explanation.walkthrough: A let in tennis is a serve that touches the net and has to be retaken, so it counts as a poor service.
explanation.definitionFit: A curl of hair is called a lock, and this word names a small curl.

clue.text: Right away, Scandinavian director was interfering

indicators.note: away means the right letter is taken out

parts.note: Norse means Scandinavian

explanation.surface: A Nordic film director meddled, giving up his rights at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' reads as immediately, but 'away' removes R from NORSE to leave NOSE, then D is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To poke one's nose in is to pry or meddle, so the past tense means meddled.

clue.text: Secret society about to retain a second posh car

indicators.note: to retain means the following pieces are held inside the word for about

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
a mo is a moment or second
RR stands for Rolls-Royce, the archetypal posh car

explanation.surface: A secret club is about to keep hold of a second luxury car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retain' splits the word for about around the rest. The Camorra is the Naples crime syndicate, Italy's counterpart of the Sicilian Mafia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neapolitan crime organisation of this name is a clandestine criminal fraternity, like the Mafia.

clue.text: Horrible duo keeping son in worn-out state

indicators.note: keeping means the son is held within the other words

parts.note: dire means dreadful or horrible
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
a duo is a pair

explanation.surface: An awful couple look after their boy in shabby surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts the son inside the word for horrible; 'worn-out state' is a noun phrase, the condition of a neglected building.
explanation.definitionFit: A building or object in poor condition through neglect is said to be in this condition.

clue.text: By the sound of it, appropriate moisture

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is spelt as it is heard, a homophone

parts.note: due means fitting or appropriate

explanation.surface: Apparently there is a suitable amount of damp.
explanation.walkthrough: DUE and the answer sound alike in most accents.
explanation.definitionFit: The droplets that condense on grass overnight are a form of moisture.

clue.text: Politician in capital making plea

indicators.note: in means the politician sits within the word for capital

parts.note: A1, written AI, means capital or first-rate
LIB is short for a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: A politician in the capital city makes an appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' here is the dated British adjective for excellent, the same as A1, written AI; 'in' places the politician inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence that the accused was elsewhere, a plea offered in court.

clue.text: Turned around ridge-like some shoes?

indicators.note: around means the turning word surrounds the ridge word

parts.note: wheeled means turned round, as a column of soldiers wheels
an edge is a ridge or sharp crest, as of a hill

explanation.surface: A woman spins round on a ridge, the kind of footwear she has on seeming apt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' looks like the anagram signal but is the synonym; 'around' wraps it round the ridge. The definition is 'like some shoes?', the hyphen in 'ridge-like' notwithstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoes with a solid wedge-shaped sole rising to the back are described by this compound adjective.

clue.text: Foreign currency from country overlooking Middle East

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so the letters for Middle East are left out

parts.note: Yemen is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: Overseas money comes from a nation looking out over the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' looks like a view from a height, but it means ignoring: drop ME from YEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the monetary unit of Japan, a currency from abroad to a British solver.
